verdict.rationale: ROS 2 is driven programmatically through documented public client-library APIs (C++ and Python) and the documented `ros2` CLI. Both expose the core capabilities: publishing and subscribing over topics, request/response services, goal/feedback/cancel actions, parameters, and a Python bag API. Missing for 10: some API features (composition, lifecycle, content filtering, intra-process communication) are C++-only, so language parity is uneven, and there is no independent hands-on corroboration of agent-driven API use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: client libraries expose to users the core functionality that makes ROS "ROS"
This verifies both the C++ and Python APIs are working properly.
Actions allow clients to send goals, receive feedback during the execution, cancel if needed, and return a result if availabl
The main entry point for the tools is the command ros2, which itself has various sub-commands for introspecting and working with nodes, topics, services, and more.
It also provides a Python API for reading from and writing to a bag from your own source code.
